paragraphs.source_en: In heat like this, even though I am only a cat, I truly cannot bear it. It is said that an Englishman named Sydney Smith, unable to endure the heat, once declared that he would like to strip off his skin and flesh and cool himself as bones alone. I do not really insist on being reduced to bones; at the very least I wish I could take off this pale gray, striped fur garment of mine and have it washed and stretched, or else pawn it for the time being. From a human point of view, cats may seem to wear the same expression year in and year out, to go through spring, summer, autumn, and winter in the same fur coat, never changing clothes, and to live lives that are simple, trouble-free, and inexpensive. In fact, we cats feel heat and cold just as others do. There are times when I would not mind taking a bath. But, you see, if one bathes in hot water while wearing this coat of fur, drying it is no easy matter, so I have no choice but to put up with being sweaty and rank. In all my life, I have never once passed through the curtain of a public bathhouse. Sometimes I have thought of getting a round fan and fanning myself, but since my paws cannot hold a fan, I have had to give up the idea. When I think of that, humans may fairly be called pampered creatures. Food that ought by rights to be eaten raw they deliberately boil, roast, dip in vinegar, smear with miso, and otherwise go to endless trouble in pursuit of mutual delight in eating. It is the same with clothing: perhaps it is asking too much of creatures born so incomplete to wear one and the same thing all year, as we cats do. Still, there is no need for them to pile such a jumble of things upon their skin. Troubling sheep, calling upon silkworms for help, and even receiving the bounty of cotton fields may well be taken as proof that their luxury is the result of their incompetence. As for food and clothing, one might overlook these things for the moment and let them pass. But when they carry on in the same way with matters that have no direct bearing on survival, it becomes quite indefensible. Take hair, for instance: since it grows naturally, the simplest method would be to leave it alone, and that would surely be best for the person concerned; yet they insist on devising all sorts of pointless schemes, cutting it into various styles and then congratulating themselves. Some people who call themselves monks always have bluish, close-shaven heads whenever one sees them. In hot weather they hold a parasol over that bare head, and in cold weather they wrap it in a hood. If that is so, why must they display that blue scalp in the first place? Then again, there are people who use a meaningless saw-toothed implement called a comb to divide their hair into two equal parts and admire themselves. Others do not divide it equally, but make some seven-to-three parting, setting up an artificial boundary across the skull. Among them are some whose part runs straight through the crown and sticks out all the way toward the back, looking exactly like a counterfeit banana leaf; how unsightly it is! Still others shave the crown flat and cut the sides straight down; though the head is round, they force a square frame onto it, so that one can only think of a cedar hedge trimmed by a gardener.

units.source_en: In heat like this, even though I am only a cat, I truly cannot bear it.
units.source_zh: 如此酷暑，我虽是只猫儿，也着实受不了。

units.source_en: It is said that an Englishman named Sydney Smith, unable to endure the heat, once declared that he would like to strip off his skin and flesh and cool himself as bones alone.

ja.t: のシドニー・スミスとか

units.source_zh: 据说有个英国人吉德尼·史密斯因为受不了暑热，曾说过真想把皮肉都除掉，只剩下骨头来凉爽凉爽。

units.source_en: I do not really insist on being reduced to bones; at the very least I wish I could take off this pale gray, striped fur garment of mine and have it washed and stretched, or else pawn it for the time being.

ja.t: りでもするか、もしくは

units.source_zh: 其实倒不一定只留下骨头，至少我希望能把我这身淡灰色带条纹的皮毛衣服脱下来洗濯一下，或者眼下把它送进当铺里去就好了。

units.source_en: In fact, we cats feel heat and cold just as others do.
units.source_zh: 其实我们猫儿也同样有冷热的感觉。

units.source_en: There are times when I would not mind taking a bath.
units.source_zh: 有时我也并不是不想洗上一次澡。

units.source_en: But, you see, if one bathes in hot water while wearing this coat of fur, drying it is no easy matter, so I have no choice but to put up with being sweaty and rank.
units.source_zh: 不过，您要知道，披着这身毛去洗热水澡，可不是那么轻易就干得了的，所以我只好耐着浑身臭汗。

units.source_en: In all my life, I have never once passed through the curtain of a public bathhouse.
units.source_zh: 我活了这么大，还没光顾过一次公共澡堂。

units.source_en: Sometimes I have thought of getting a round fan and fanning myself, but since my paws cannot hold a fan, I have had to give up the idea.

ja.t: らんではないが、とにかく

units.source_zh: 有时我也不是没有想过，弄把团扇来扇扇，无奈我的爪子拿不住扇子，也就只好打消了这个念头。

units.source_en: When I think of that, humans may fairly be called pampered creatures.
units.source_zh: 想起来，人可谓太养尊处优了。

units.source_en: Food that ought by rights to be eaten raw they deliberately boil, roast, dip in vinegar, smear with miso, and otherwise go to endless trouble in pursuit of mutual delight in eating.

ja.t: ってしかるべきものをわざわざ

units.source_zh: 本来应该生吃的食物，却要煮着吃、烧着吃，又是蘸着醋吃，又是蘸着酱吃，绝不嫌麻烦，想方设法来大享口福。

units.source_en: It is the same with clothing: perhaps it is asking too much of creatures born so incomplete to wear one and the same thing all year, as we cats do.
units.source_zh: 穿衣服也是如此，要求他们像我们猫儿那样一年到头总穿着同一件衣服，对于他们这种生来就残缺不全者说来，也许是过高的要求。

units.source_en: Still, there is no need for them to pile such a jumble of things upon their skin.
units.source_zh: 不过，也毫无必要像他们那样在皮肤上再蒙上那么杂七杂八的东西呀。

units.source_en: Troubling sheep, calling upon silkworms for help, and even receiving the bounty of cotton fields may well be taken as proof that their luxury is the result of their incompetence.
units.source_zh: 又是给羊添麻烦，又是请蚕来帮忙，甚至还要托棉田的福，这满可以认为是他们既奢侈又无能的结果。

units.source_en: As for food and clothing, one might overlook these things for the moment and let them pass.
units.source_zh: 对于衣食方面，还可以姑且原谅他们，不去计较。

units.source_en: But when they carry on in the same way with matters that have no direct bearing on survival, it becomes quite indefensible.

ja.t: もないところまでこの

units.source_zh: 但对于生存上毫无直接利害关系方面，他们也要照此办理，就太说不过去了。

units.source_en: Take hair, for instance: since it grows naturally, the simplest method would be to leave it alone, and that would surely be best for the person concerned;

ja.t: のためになるだろうと

units.source_zh: 先说头发吧，它是自然生长的，本来最便当的办法就是不去管它，而且对本人也有好处；

units.source_en: yet they insist on devising all sorts of pointless schemes, cutting it into various styles and then congratulating themselves.
units.source_zh: 可他们偏偏硬要想一些馊主意，剪成各种发型而自鸣得意。

units.source_en: Some people who call themselves monks always have bluish, close-shaven heads whenever one sees them.
units.source_zh: 有一些自称是什么和尚的人，不管何时看去，总是青光光的脑袋。

units.source_en: In hot weather they hold a parasol over that bare head, and in cold weather they wrap it in a hood.
units.source_zh: 热天他们在光头上撑把伞，冷天又用头巾把脑袋包起来。

units.source_en: If that is so, why must they display that blue scalp in the first place?
units.source_zh: 既然这样，他们又何必非得展示他们的青头皮不可呢？

units.source_en: Then again, there are people who use a meaningless saw-toothed implement called a comb to divide their hair into two equal parts and admire themselves.
units.source_zh: 另外，还有一种叫做木梳的、毫无意义的锯齿状的工具，人用它来把头发分成两等分，进行自我欣赏。

units.source_en: Others do not divide it equally, but make some seven-to-three parting, setting up an artificial boundary across the skull.
units.source_zh: 有的不做两等分，而是搞什么三七分，在头盖骨上搞起个人工区划。

units.source_en: Among them are some whose part runs straight through the crown and sticks out all the way toward the back, looking exactly like a counterfeit banana leaf; how unsightly it is!

ja.t: しているのがある。まるで

units.source_zh: 他们当中有的人的分头恰好通过头上的旋儿，结果一直向后直愣着，活像个破芭蕉叶儿，您说多难看！

units.source_en: Still others shave the crown flat and cut the sides straight down; though the head is round, they force a square frame onto it, so that one can only think of a cedar hedge trimmed by a gardener.
units.source_zh: 还有的头顶上平推，两旁却直着剪下去，本来脑袋是圆的，却硬要镶成一个方框框，只能让人联想花匠剪过的杉篱笆。

paragraphs.source_zh: 如此酷暑，我虽是只猫儿，也着实受不了。据说有个英国人吉德尼·史密斯因为受不了暑热，曾说过真想把皮肉都除掉，只剩下骨头来凉爽凉爽。其实倒不一定只留下骨头，至少我希望能把我这身淡灰色带条纹的皮毛衣服脱下来洗濯一下，或者眼下把它送进当铺里去就好了。拿人的眼光来看，也许觉得我们猫儿成年累月总是一个表情，春夏秋冬总是穿着这身毛衣，永不换装，过着又省事又不费钱的日子。其实我们猫儿也同样有冷热的感觉。有时我也并不是不想洗上一次澡。不过，您要知道，披着这身毛去洗热水澡，可不是那么轻易就干得了的，所以我只好耐着浑身臭汗。我活了这么大，还没光顾过一次公共澡堂。有时我也不是没有想过，弄把团扇来扇扇，无奈我的爪子拿不住扇子，也就只好打消了这个念头。想起来，人可谓太养尊处优了。本来应该生吃的食物，却要煮着吃、烧着吃，又是蘸着醋吃，又是蘸着酱吃，绝不嫌麻烦，想方设法来大享口福。穿衣服也是如此，要求他们像我们猫儿那样一年到头总穿着同一件衣服，对于他们这种生来就残缺不全者说来，也许是过高的要求。不过，也毫无必要像他们那样在皮肤上再蒙上那么杂七杂八的东西呀。又是给羊添麻烦，又是请蚕来帮忙，甚至还要托棉田的福，这满可以认为是他们既奢侈又无能的结果。对于衣食方面，还可以姑且原谅他们，不去计较。但对于生存上毫无直接利害关系方面，他们也要照此办理，就太说不过去了。先说头发吧，它是自然生长的，本来最便当的办法就是不去管它，而且对本人也有好处；可他们偏偏硬要想一些馊主意，剪成各种发型而自鸣得意。有一些自称是什么和尚的人，不管何时看去，总是青光光的脑袋。热天他们在光头上撑把伞，冷天又用头巾把脑袋包起来。既然这样，他们又何必非得展示他们的青头皮不可呢？另外，还有一种叫做木梳的、毫无意义的锯齿状的工具，人用它来把头发分成两等分，进行自我欣赏。有的不做两等分，而是搞什么三七分，在头盖骨上搞起个人工区划。他们当中有的人的分头恰好通过头上的旋儿，结果一直向后直愣着，活像个破芭蕉叶儿，您说多难看！还有的头顶上平推，两旁却直着剪下去，本来脑袋是圆的，却硬要镶成一个方框框，只能让人联想花匠剪过的杉篱笆。
